You are a parallel engineering worker on the ESP32-S31 openvela project. Workspace: /home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela. The user explicitly requested parallel agents, prioritizing working hardware/BLE and a coherent final product demo. Read the applicable instructions and evidence. Do not access serial devices, USB/IP, flash either board, reset hardware, start heavy whole-firmware builds, edit maintained source/shared configs, edit the checklist, or modify previous evidence. The root owns board and build sequencing. Rootfs has <350 MiB free; write only to the assigned D-drive task directory. Read existing backups selectively; never recursively search all backups or the entire source tree. Do not expose credentials or dump raw private pairing material. Keep original test failures intact and distinguish separate firmware evidence from same-image integration. No publishing or communication to humans. Produce concrete reviewed files/patches and a concise result, not just an unexecuted plan. The root is building E400 cache-writeback-execution, normal korvo-smp-services with 17 ELFs. E399 started all four AppFS services then CPU0 faulted at Flash-resident esp32s31_writeback_all_locked. E400 moves exactly that helper to IRAM. Do not mutate those inputs. E398 BLE simultaneous advertising/scanning and E393 RPA pairing 20/20 passed, both single-core FLAT. Existing E166 and E159 single-core product demos are archived and verified but do not prove BLE inclusion.

Assigned output directory: /mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/parallel-product-convergence-e401/image_pipeline

Advance the unfinished JPEG encode/decode and RGB888 product-size functionality. Inspect maintained code and the exact existing U03/U04/U06 evidence; find actual codec entry points and current 2x2 limitations. In your task directory prepare a minimal source patch/candidate and meaningful host verification with product-sized synthetic images, decode dimensions/pixels and proper failure cleanup, only where it exercises real maintained implementations. Do not mirror implementation-only tests or claim target camera/DMA acceptance from host results. Avoid adding dependencies or network downloads. Keep all changes private for root integration because a firmware build is live. Deliver concrete code/patch, validation output, and the shortest owned-Korvo target check required. No hardware access or heavy full build.

I’ll read the workspace instructions and exact U03/U04/U06 evidence, then prepare a minimal candidate patch and host validation in the assigned D-drive directory. I’ll leave maintained files, live build inputs, and hardware untouched.

The maintained `jpegtest` only checks a fixed 2×2 image. It uses the real libjpeg-turbo APIs, but pixel validation covers only the first decoded pixel, and codec errors use libjpeg’s default process-exit handler. I’ll extend that command with product-sized synthetic images, full pixel checks, and recoverable error handling.

E05 confirms the historical 2×2 pass, and its earlier failed run remains intact. I also found that the decoder can warn and synthesize an end marker for truncated input. The candidate treats that warning as a failure and bounds the encoder’s output buffer so error cleanup retains clear ownership. Host validation will use a private build of the maintained codec sources.

The candidate passes full pixel checks at 320×240, 640×480, 800×480, and odd-sized 641×479 under host ASan/UBSan. Each case also rejects seven malformed or bounded-output cases and completes a valid decode afterward. I’m adding allocation-failure sweeps and independent color checks. LeakSanitizer cannot run under this environment’s ptrace restriction; that failure is preserved, and cleanup will be checked with allocation accounting.

Independent checks now confirm the RGB channel order and RGB565 primary values, plus rejection of truncated files, oversized headers, and a valid JPEG with the wrong pixels. Single-pixel, single-row, single-column, and 1920×1080 cases also pass. The row checks cover padded scanline storage; external camera-frame stride and DMA remain untested. The allocation sweeps and 100-cycle product-size run are still running.

Both allocation checks passed: all 17 encoder and 10 decoder allocation failure points returned cleanly, and 100 cycles at 800×480 left zero tracked allocations. Peak requested host heap was 1,223,674 bytes. I’m finalizing the private patch, reproducible validation bundle, and Korvo check. The evidence review used the `xts-board-evidence` skill to keep E05’s historical result separate from final-product acceptance.

Prepared a reviewed private [patch]( /mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/parallel-product-convergence-e401/image_pipeline/jpeg-product-size.patch) extending maintained `jpegtest` with product dimensions, full pixel checks, truncation rejection, and failure cleanup.

Host validation passed through 1920×1080, including 27 allocation-failure points and 100×800×480 cycles with zero retained allocations. ASan/UBSan passed; cleanup used allocation accounting because LeakSanitizer was unavailable.

[Validation and reproduction](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/parallel-product-convergence-e401/image_pipeline/README.md) · [Root integration and Korvo check](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/parallel-product-convergence-e401/image_pipeline/final-handoff.md)

Shortest target workload: `jpegtest`, then `jpegtest 800 480 3`, bracketed by heap/service observations.

Maintained files, E400 inputs, historical evidence, and hardware remain untouched. Host results do not establish camera/DMA or same-image acceptance.
